newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ex-Thai PM Anand wins Magsaysay prize.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Thai PM Anand wins Magsaysay prize.

text.p: Former Thai prime minister Anand Panyarachun has won the 1997 Ramon Magsaysay Award for government service for his campaign to strengthen democracy and stamp out corruption in Thailand, the award foundation said on Thursday.
Anand is the 16th Thai to win the Magsaysay prize since it was established in 1958 to perpetuate the memory of a popular former Philippine president who died in an air crash in 1957.
He was selected for the award for "sustaining the momentum for reform and democracy in Thailand in a time of crisis and military rule", the foundation said in its citation.

Appointed twice as interim prime minister, Anand expanded press freedom, promoted privatisation, tax reform and trade liberalisation which "stoked the country's economy and helped win the confidence of investors at home and abroad", it said.

"As a leading member of the assembly drafting his country's new constitution, he has laboured to strengthen democracy in Thailand by securing civil liberties, making government more accountable to citizens and eliminating vote-buying and other scourges of money politics," the citation added.
"It is no longer in question whether we should opt for economic development or democracy," it quoted Anand as saying. "The two must proceed together."
Anand, a former career diplomat and now a business leader, will receive a gold medallion and a cash prize of $50,000 in ceremonies in Manila in August.
The foundation has yet to name the winners for public service, community leadership, international understanding and journalism, literature and creative communication arts.
